findings.text: The first sentence tells a newcomer what Athena is, and the second says what sets it apart. They could describe it after a few seconds of reading.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: The page explains why it exists, and every statement has a cited source that links to exact lines at a pinned commit, so the reader can check the claim for themselves.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The lede says Athena's job is changing code, but the page only shows Athena reading and explaining a project. A newcomer never sees the core product, a request turned into a change, so the case for why Athena matters to them is weak.
findings.source: <h1> "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and lede "turns a short request into a change to a code repository"

findings.text: A jump link near the top leads straight to the next steps, which are clear: a repository link, an install command and a sample request. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" (header) and the Next steps section

findings.text: The install step gives no clone command and no prerequisites (a Rust toolchain? model API keys?). It also doesn't say what `athena ask` will produce or change, so a newcomer must leave the page before they can safely try it.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: Most of the page covers firstmate internals, such as exit codes, the places-held counter and teardown edge cases. That depth serves someone studying firstmate, but a newcomer who came to learn about Athena will have to skim most of it.
The Start here section has a short orientation, a one-task walkthrough and terms defined before use. This makes the firstmate material much easier to follow for a stranger.
The note doesn't say which repository holds `studies/`, so a newcomer can't tell where to find the source data or how to make a study of their own.
findings.source: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The page states openly that the study never ran firstmate and only read its files. This helps a newcomer judge how far to trust the explanation.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."
